title: Parmesan Focaccia with a Potato Dough
changes_from_base: Cooked mashed potato in a slightly smaller dough and a grated Parmesan crust instead of flaky salt.
summary: An extra-soft focaccia made with mashed potato in the dough and baked under a lacy crust of grated cheese.
equipment: cling film or a clean tea towel

ingredients.item: floury potato (such as Maris Piper or russet), peeled and cut into 3 cm chunks

ingredients.note: potato cooking water topped up with plain water, about 38 °C

steps.title: Potato
steps.text: Cover the chunks with cold unsalted water, bring to the boil and simmer 12-15 min, until a knife slides through. Drain, saving 150 ml of the cloudy water, and rice or mash until smooth; leave until just warm. Starch from the potato holds on to water, which keeps the crumb soft for longer.

steps.title: Dough
steps.text: Mix the flour and yeast, then add the potato, the 300 ml warm liquid and 2 tbsp oil and stir 2 min into a soft, tacky dough. Rest 15 min, add the salt and squeeze it in.

steps.title: Folds
steps.text: Give the dough three sets of folds 30 min apart, stretching each side up and over the centre. It will feel silkier than a plain dough.

steps.title: Tin
steps.text: Spread 2 tbsp oil over the tin, tip in the dough, turn it to coat and press it towards the corners. Cover and leave about 1 h, until puffy, nudging it into the corners halfway.

steps.title: Top
steps.text: Heat the oven to 220 °C (200 °C fan). Drizzle the last 1 tbsp oil, dimple deeply with your fingertips, then cover evenly with the cheese and the pepper.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake 22-25 min, until the cheese is lacy and golden and the edges are crisp; the centre reads about 96 °C. Cool 15 min on a rack before slicing into 12.

tips: Use a floury potato; waxy ones make a gluey mash.
Let the potato cool to just warm before mixing or it can weaken the yeast.
A common mistake is piling the cheese in the centre; spread it right to the edges so every slice gets a crisp top.
storage: Keep wrapped at room temperature for 1 day, then in the fridge for up to 3 days. Reheat at 200 °C for 5-6 min; freeze for up to 1 month. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
